title: fix(plugin-hono-server,hono,cloud-connection)!: refuse an unparseable request body with 400 INVALID_REQUEST instead of reading it as {}
body:
Fixes #23914

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What

A request body that an HTTP door cannot parse is now refused with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` and the ADR-0112 envelope. It is no longer handed to the handler as `{}`. `INVALID_REQUEST` is an existing `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` code; no code or ledger row is added. The message names the failure and never echoes the body.

| package | door | what changed |
|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` | `HonoHttpServer.runHandler` (every route registered through `IHttpServer`, plus the fallback seam): the `objectstack dev` / `os serve` door | `req.body` is an accessor. Reading a body the adapter could not parse throws the refusal, and the adapter answers it whatever the handler made of the throw |
| `@objectstack/hono` | `createHonoApp`'s `readDispatchBody`, used by the `${prefix}/*` catch-all and the `/auth/*` legacy fallback | a body declared `application/json` that is not blank and does not parse is refused when the dispatched domain READS it, after the dispatcher's gates; a domain that forwards the request reads its own bytes and answers as before |
| `@objectstack/cloud-connection` | its own Hono routes: `/bind/start`, `/bind/poll`, `/install`, and `marketplace/install-local` | same rule, through a module-private `readJsonRequestBody` |

## Measured at the door

These are fresh `objectstack dev --seed-admin` showcase boots, base `2054a0888c` against `b9df5b1d3` (`origin/main` merged in; the same answers were read on `0660b5a16` before the merge). This door is `plugin-hono-server`, which is byte-identical at the current head `97d881a2e`. Every body was sent from a file with `curl --data-binary`. The admin session came from `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email`.

| request | base | head |
|---|---|---|
| step 1, `POST /data/showcase_account/query` `{"where": {"status": "churned"}}` | 200, 2 rows | 200, 2 rows |
| step 2, the same with the closing brace missing | **200, 14 of 14 rows** | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` "The request body could not be parsed as JSON (it was sent as application/json). …" |
| step 3, `{ not json` | **200, 14 rows** | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, same message |
| step 4, the valid where-body sent as `text/plain` | **200, 14 rows** | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` "The request body was sent as text/plain, which this server does not read into a request body. …" |
| step 5, `PATCH /data/showcase_account/ID` `{"name": "HACKED"` | **200**, name unchanged, `updated_at` bumped | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`; name and `updated_at` unchanged |
| step 6, `POST /data/showcase_account` truncated, with `name` | 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` "Account Name is required" | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, the parse refusal |
| CONTROL: empty body, `application/json` | 200, 14 rows (empty query) | 200, 14 rows |
| CONTROL: `POST` with no body and no `Content-Type` | 200, 14 rows | 200, 14 rows |
| CONTROL: valid `PATCH` / valid create / empty-body create | 200 / 201 / 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 200 / 201 / 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` |
| CONTROL: presign then raw `PUT` of a `.txt` file as `text/plain`, then complete | 200 / 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 / 200 |
| CONTROL: presign then raw `PUT` of a JSON-with-comments file as `application/json`, then complete | 200 / 200 / 200 | 200 / 200 / 200 |
| dispatcher-bridged doors (`0660b5a16`): `PUT /meta/object/showcase_account`, `POST /keys`, truncated | (not run on base) | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, the parse refusal |
| `POST /cloud-connection/bind/poll` truncated `{"device_code": "dc_1"` / `{}` | (not run on base) | 400 the parse refusal / 400 "device_code is required" (unchanged) |
| `POST /marketplace/install-local` truncated `{"packageId": "com.example.crm"` | (not run on base) | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, the parse refusal |

On this boot the door is served by `plugin-hono-server`. `createHonoApp` (`@objectstack/hono`) is the embed door, and nothing in `packages/cli` mounts it. Both transports carried the swallow, so both change, as triage asked.

## Why `plugin-hono-server` refuses when `req.body` is read, not before the handler runs

The PM's mechanism assumption 3 ("who else relies on `{}`") was measured, and it moved the design. One transport serves JSON doors and byte doors, and only the route knows which one it is:

- The storage presign answers `headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }` for a `.json` file, so the platform's own upload flow PUTs a JSON-with-comments file (a `tsconfig.json`, say) as declared JSON that does not parse. The raw-PUT route reads `req.rawBody()` and stores it with `200` (measured on both boots above). objectui's `UploadProvider` sends `Content-Type: mimeType` on that PUT.
- The dogfood suites PUT raw bytes as `text/plain` (`attachments-authz-harness.ts`, `field-file-collection`, and others).

Refusing before the handler would have turned both uploads into `400`s. Raised on read, the refusal reaches exactly the handlers that would otherwise have acted on an invented `{}`, and it stops them at the read, so nothing after it runs and nothing is written. Body presence for the media types the adapter does not read is judged by the RFC 9112 framing headers (`Content-Length` other than `0`, or `Transfer-Encoding`). Reading the bytes to find out would buffer an upload before storage's declared-length check refuses it. Reading `Request.body` cannot answer either, because `@hono/node-server` gives every non-GET/HEAD request a stream.

## One rule on both transports: the reader refuses (seat ruling B)

`createHonoApp` follows the same rule. Its body is a `dispatch()` argument rather than a `req` property, so for a declared-JSON body that does not parse, `readDispatchBody` hands `dispatch()` a body value whose every read (a property, `in`, its keys, a spread, `JSON.stringify`) throws `RequestBodyRefusal` and records that it was read. Each arm (the `${prefix}/*` catch-all and the `/auth/*` legacy fallback) then answers that refusal if, and only if, the body was read, whatever the domain answered. This is the same override `plugin-hono-server` applies after its `req.body` getter. There is no new export and no list of routes: whether a domain reads the body is answered by the domain reading it.

- `dispatch()` itself never reads `body`. Its liveness short-circuit, scope resolution, the ADR-0069 auth gate and project membership read the path and headers, and `body` goes straight to the domain's handler. So the gates still answer first, as they do ahead of a route handler on `plugin-hono-server`.
- A domain that forwards the request reads its own bytes and never touches `body`: `/webhooks/redeliver`, the inbound automation hooks, and the `/approvals/act` form `POST`. It answers exactly as at base, a malformed body included, after its own sign-in or signature check. `hono-webhooks-redeliver.conformance.test.ts`'s `not JSON` row, which holds the hosted door byte-equal to the self-hosted mount, stays as pinned and is green.

`b9df5b1d3` refused before `dispatch()` instead. That reddened exactly that row: the hosted door answered this adapter's message where the mount answers the member's `"Request body must be JSON."`. It also answered an anonymous caller `400` where the mount says `401`. The seat's contract review ruled B.

## Step 4 (`text/plain`): refuse, not parse

`content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx` documents the contract: "All requests and responses use `application/json`", and `Content-Type: application/json` is a required request header. Parsing `text/plain` as JSON would be a lenient second dialect. On `plugin-hono-server` it would also mean reading every text upload eagerly. So step 4 is refused there. `createHonoApp` was already content-type-blind (it parses a `text/plain` body as JSON when it parses), and that is unchanged. See Acceptance notes.

## Which doors treat an empty body as `{}`, legitimately

All three keep it. A blank or whitespace-only body declared as JSON, and a request with no body whatever it declares, are still `{}`. The REST query handler documents the reliance ("An empty request body is not `null`: the HTTP adapter hands it over as `{}`, an empty query"). Bodiless action `POST`s rely on it too (`/bind/start`, `/automation/NAME/trigger`). The empty-body controls above and in every suite pin it.

## Sibling sweep (lane `domain:cli`)

The sweep covered `.json().catch(`, `catch {}` around a body parse, and `return {}` from a body reader, over `packages/{cli,runtime,verify,types,rest,mcp,observability,client*,cloud-connection,create-objectstack,adapters/*,qa}` plus `plugin-hono-server` and `plugin-dev`.

In scope (a door that takes a client body), changed here:
- `plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts` `runHandler`: the `c.req.json()` / `parseBody()` pair.
- `adapters/hono/src/index.ts` `readDispatchBody`: both `{}` fallbacks, which serve both arms.
- `cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts`: `/bind/start`, `/bind/poll`, `/install`.
- `cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`: `handleInstall`.

Out, with the reason:
- `cloud-connection-plugin.ts` `tokResp.json().catch`, `bindResp.json().catch` and the install relay's `resp.json().catch`: these read the cloud control plane's answers, a body the platform wrote itself.
- `packages/qa/http-conformance/src/adapter.ts` `NodeHttpServer` (`catch { body = {} }`): `private: true`, ships nothing, and serves only the conformance suite's own requests. It is a reference harness, not a deployed door (Acceptance notes).
- `packages/qa/http-conformance` itself (this lane) gains `src/hono-body-refusal.conformance.test.ts`, which pins ruling B against the real dispatcher (Tests).
- `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:1314`: a comment, not a body reader. It describes the catch-all's pre-#22576 line. Its point, that falsy JSON values arrive falsy, still holds, so `meta.ts` is untouched.

Not in this lane, so not changed here: the same swallow in `plugin-auth`, measured at the door. Truncated `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/unlock-user` `{"userId": "usr_nobody"` answers `400 "userId is required"`. That is reported to the seat. `plugin-webhooks` already refuses ("Request body must be JSON."). `metadata`'s HMR reload reads a body the CLI's own watch loop posts.

## Tests

All runs are under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, with each exit code captured before any pipe. The current head is `97d881a2e`: `b9df5b1d3` (which merges `origin/main` at `adce19297`) plus ruling B in `@objectstack/hono`, its pins, and the corrected `hono` changeset. `plugin-hono-server` and `cloud-connection` are byte-identical to `b9df5b1d3`, so their runs there stand.

- Ruling B on `0cee7c3d9` (the code of `97d881a2e`, whose last commit only rewrites the `hono` changeset):
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/hono exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 9 files, 180 passed.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/http-conformance exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 14 files, 150 passed, including the redeliver row as pinned.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/hono typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/http-conformance typecheck`: exit 0.
- `@objectstack/http-conformance` at the merge base `adce19297` (a detached compare worktree, closure built there): 13 files, 144 passed. At `b9df5b1d3` it was 1 failed, 143 passed: `hono-webhooks-redeliver.conformance.test.ts` line 273, row `not JSON`.
- `pnpm turbo run build --filter='!@objectstack/docs' --concurrency=2` on `97d881a2e`: exit 0, 75 tasks.

- After the merge (AGENTS.md §9/§10): `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exit 0; `pnpm turbo run build --filter='!@objectstack/docs' --concurrency=2` exit 0, 75 tasks; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server typecheck` on `b9df5b1d3`: exit 0, including `check:test-typecheck` OK. `@objectstack/hono` exit 0 and `@objectstack/cloud-connection` exit 0, each `tsc --noEmit` plus `-p tsconfig.test.json`.
- On `b9df5b1d3`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 30 files, 386 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/hono exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 9 files, 176 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cloud-connection exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 46 files, 561 passed.

New pins:
- `plugin-hono-server/src/request-body-refusal.test.ts` (20 cases):
  - each card body refused, with the envelope parsed against `ApiErrorSchema` / `envelopeViolations`, the handler never acting, and no echo;
  - the handler's own catch arm answering 500 loses to the refusal;
  - the fallback seam both ways;
  - a real socket for step 4;
  - CONTROL: valid, empty, form, valid PATCH, and three byte doors stored byte for byte.
- `adapters/hono/src/hono-body-refusal.test.ts` (18 cases), over a fixture dispatcher with a READER domain (reads `body` inside a `try` whose catch answers its own 500) and a FORWARDER (reads the forwarded request):
  - the card bodies refused 400 by the reader, though it answered 500;
  - a read that escapes `dispatch()`;
  - the `/auth/*` fallback, `DELETE` included;
  - the forwarder answering its own refusal with every byte;
  - CONTROL rows;
  - parity with `HonoHttpServer`.
- `packages/qa/http-conformance/src/hono-body-refusal.conformance.test.ts` (6 cases), on the real dispatcher and data domain through `createHonoApp`:
  - steps 2, 3, 5 and 6 refused, with the store read back unchanged;
  - byte parity with a `HonoHttpServer` route;
  - order: an active ADR-0069 gate whose session read fails answers 503, not the body's 400;
  - CONTROL: a valid query filters, and an empty body is the empty query.
- `hono-catch-all-raw-request.test.ts` gains the case that a declared-JSON body that does not parse still reaches a forwarding domain unread, byte for byte.
- `cloud-connection`: four refusal cases plus an empty-body CONTROL in `error-envelope.conformance.test.ts`. In `marketplace-install-local-install-modes.test.ts`, a refusal with zero writes (no register, no sync, no import, no ledger entry), plus a CONTROL.
- Fixture triage: `hono-catch-all-raw-request.test.ts`'s `['invalid JSON', 'application/json', '{ not json', {}]` row pinned the branch this removes, so it is replaced. The refusal moved to the new file, and the row now pins the undeclared spelling, which is unchanged.

## Ablation (one per package; every suite resolves its subject from source, so no rebuild)

Each leg ran through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, with the anchor hitting once, the write proven on disk, and the restore proven.

| leg | mutation | blob | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| plugin-hono-server | the accessor's refusal branch becomes `return {}` | `a331a0f6ed81` to `dee7fcca5045` | 10 failed: every refusal case, the fallback-reads case, socket step 4. 10 passed: every CONTROL |
| hono, swallow (on `0cee7c3d9`) | `refusedOnRead(…)` becomes `readable({})` | `fb199e0ebefb` to `9c5714c12488` | `hono`: 10 failed (every reader refusal, the escaping read, `/auth/*`, parity), 8 passed. http-conformance: 4 failed (steps 2, 3, 5 and 6, parity), 9 passed (the order case, CONTROL, and every redeliver row) |
| hono, refuse before `dispatch()` (the `b9df5b1d3` shape, on `0cee7c3d9`) | `refusedOnRead(…)` becomes an immediate throw | `fb199e0ebefb` to `4f27b2629aad` | `hono`: 7 failed (the reader-ownership cases, `/auth/*`, the forwarder), 11 passed. http-conformance: 2 failed (the redeliver byte-parity row and the gate-order case), 11 passed |
| cloud-connection (on `2d952cae1`, the file unchanged since) | the `ok: false` parse refusal becomes `{ ok: true, body: {} }` | `61561f4f3e17` to `7c27524a66d0` | 4 failed: the four refusals. 41 passed, including both empty-body CONTROLs |

The plugin-hono-server leg ran on `0660b5a16`, and its file is byte-identical at the current head. Restore proof after each run: `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes and `git status --porcelain` is 0 lines. Each file's `git hash-object` equals its `HEAD:` blob (`a331a0f6ed81…`, `fb199e0ebefb…`, `61561f4f3e17…`), and the marker count is 0.

## Gates

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on `97d881a2e` (no paths, merge base `adce19297`): 66 families. All 66 ran and every one exited 0, including `check:route-envelope`, `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`, `check:error-status-conformance`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:published-files`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:empty-changeset` and `check-changeset-no-major`. `--ran` reconciliation with `COMMAND :: exit CODE` records: "66 derived, 66 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".
- The derivation flags one stale input: `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` changed on `main` after the merge base (`d132140eb`, #23050 slice 10). That change only moves declared counts from `rest-server.ts` to the new `ui-routes.ts`, and this diff touches neither. The branch is merge-clean against `origin/main`, so it is not merged (`git merge-tree` exit 0).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/http-conformance test` (the suite that went red in CI's `Test Core (3/6)` on `b9df5b1d3`): base `adce19297` 13 files, 144 passed; head 14 files, 150 passed.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the 12 changed `.ts` files: exit 0, no findings. The repo-wide run is CI's `Lint & Repo Gates`.
- On `0660b5a16`, the first sweep reddened `check:route-envelope`: the new `cloud-connection` helper built a response, so the gate wanted a `PLUGIN_ROUTE_MODULES` row. That script is outside this card's file surface, so the helper now answers a message and each declared route module builds its own `400` body.

## Acceptance notes

- **`createHonoApp` reads every content type as JSON.** This is pre-existing and unchanged. A JSON body sent as `text/plain` is parsed (step 4 is honoured there, not refused), and a non-JSON body that does not declare JSON is `{}`. The reader-refuses mechanism could carry that input too, but it would narrow a second input and is not this card's. Carrier: none.
- **Three copies of one message.** The refusal text lives in `plugin-hono-server/src/request-body.ts`, `adapters/hono/src/index.ts` and `cloud-connection/src/request-json-body.ts`, each module-private. A shared export would enlarge a package's public surface, which this card's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` does not declare. The hono parity case holds the two transports' answers equal.
- **`@objectstack/http-conformance`'s `NodeHttpServer`** keeps its `catch { body = {} }`. It is a private reference harness. The suites do drive a malformed body: `hono-webhooks-redeliver`'s `not JSON` row and the new `hono-body-refusal` file, both through the two Hono doors. Neither drives one through `NodeHttpServer`. (The v1 sentence said no suite drives a malformed body at all, which was false.)
- **`runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:1314`'s comment** still quotes the catch-all's pre-#22576 line, `c.req.json().catch(() => ({}))`. Its subject (falsy JSON values arrive falsy) is still true.
- **Ordering.** On both Hono transports the refusal comes from the body's reader, so every gate ahead of the reader answers first: the dispatcher's gates on `createHonoApp`, and a route's own checks on `plugin-hono-server`. On `cloud-connection`'s `/bind/start` and `/bind/poll`, the body is read before the session check, as it always was. Neither refusal discloses anything.

## Contract review

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: the seat serves the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review before the queue. Three changesets (`.changeset/23914-*.md`) are `minor` under the launch-window convention for breaking changes. Each carries the `Clause-②` line, an ADR-0087 marker of kind `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with the other categories closed on facts, and the FROM / TO for an integrator.
